_comment: Effective file-size bits-per-weight for llama.cpp quantization types.
These are whole-file averages: K-quants keep some tensors (output, attn_v,
parts of ffn_down) at higher precision, so the average sits above the
nominal block width. Models with very large vocabularies (Llama 3 at
128k, Gemma at 256k) land a few percent higher again because the
embedding and output matrices are a big share of the parameters.
Q4_K_M is pinned to a real measurement: Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Q4_K_M
`svrspec verify` re-measures against whatever GGUF files are present and
reports the error, so these stay honest.

entries.notes: Only worth considering when RAM is the hard constraint; noticeably worse instruction following.
Measurable quality loss on structured extraction tasks.
Smaller than Q4_K_M at similar quality, but slower on CPU: the i-quant dot products are more expensive.
Default choice for CPU deployment. Best quality-per-byte-read, and decode is bandwidth bound.
About 16% more bytes read per token than Q4_K_M, so decode is ~16% slower.
Rarely justified on CPU: costs a third more bandwidth than Q4_K_M for a barely measurable quality gain.
Useful as a quality reference baseline, and fast per-byte on AVX-512-VNNI / AMX-INT8 for prefill.
Only for accuracy comparison. Halves decode speed versus Q8_0 and quadruples it versus Q4_K_M.
